dataset_family: RECOGNISED (EU Horizon 2020 multicentre observational study of adults aged 65+ with type 2 diabetes; 11 clinical sites in 7 European countries; NCT04281186). Cross-sectional baseline: 307 people (578 eyes), 182 MCI vs 125 normal cognition. No other corpus block reports RECOGNISED.
method_family: Colour fundus photography (mydriatic, disc-centred ETDRS field, six camera models across centres) with semi-automated retinal vessel morphometry (VAMPIRE-Web: CRAE, CRVE, AVR, tortuosity, fractal dimension), graded by one masked grader. Crude and multivariable logistic regression with cluster-robust SEs (both eyes) and ROC/AUC.
what_it_shows: Pedersen, Lois, Biessels, Exalto, Perez-Hoyos, Simo and Grauslund 2026, Primary Care Diabetes. The MCI reference is a 13-test battery plus mCDR. In univariable models, venular width (CRVE) and arteriolar tortuosity were associated with MCI. After adjustment only arteriolar tortuosity remained (OR 1.44 per SD, 95% CI 1.08-1.92). The paper describes the direction as 'the less the tortuosity the higher the risk'. The other seven parameters were not associated. All retinal parameters together gave AUC 0.62. The clinical covariates alone gave AUC 0.66 (Table 2 reference). Retinal parameters plus covariates gave AUC 0.73. The authors call this 'acceptable' but say it 'still falls short of strong discriminative accuracy'. Before clinical use they require full automation and an AUC of at least 0.80. They also warn of spurious associations from multiple testing.
why:
PDF identity confirmed. The title, the seven named authors plus the RECOGNISED Study Group, and DOI 10.1016/j.pcd.2026.02.004 all match the block header and its source metadata. I read the whole extract (pp.1-5, up to the References). The block's corrected Results field matches the PDF. Its Problems/Improvements/Gaps fields still contain the flagged fabrication and contradict the PDF: OCTA, 'single-center cohort' and 'AUC 0.72-0.78 for vessel density'. This verdict relies only on the PDF.

STATED FORM, partly. The part it shows: in its own multicentre data, one retinal-structure measure (arteriolar tortuosity on colour fundus photographs) is independently associated with MCI in older adults with type 2 diabetes. That is evidence for retinal structure as a biomarker direction for early cognitive decline. What it does not show:
(a) Retinal structure on its own discriminates poorly (AUC 0.62, p.4). The 0.73 quoted in the block needs age, education, DR severity and other covariates, and the covariates alone reach 0.66.
(b) Scalability is not demonstrated. The analysis is semi-automated, and the authors list full automation and AUC >= 0.80 as preconditions (p.5).
(c) The evidence is thin: 1 of 8 parameters survived adjustment, and the authors flag multiple testing.
(d) The population is T2D only, with strict exclusions (p.5 limitation).
It says nothing about eye movements.

An internal inconsistency a reviewer should know about (my reading of Table 2, not the paper's words). The arteriolar tortuosity row gives crude OR 1.31 (1.01-1.71) together with a crude AUC of 0.48. A single-predictor logistic model with a significant positive OR should not give an AUC below 0.5. Separately, the text says lower tortuosity means higher risk, while the OR is > 1 per SD increment. The paper does not reconcile the direction. The tortuosity analyses also rest on 315 of 578 eyes.

NARROWED FORM, partly. It fits the core of the narrowed wording: a preliminary association of an ocular measure with MCI, not externally validated and not shown to be scalable. It does not fit the wording as drafted:
- It is multicentre, not single-centre.
- It is restricted to type 2 diabetes (a different population).
- Its retinal-only discrimination (AUC 0.62) is weaker than the 'discriminated MCI' wording used for P-5/P-952.
Admitting it would require wording such as 'lower arteriolar tortuosity on fundus photographs was associated with MCI in a European multicentre type 2 diabetes cohort, with weak stand-alone discrimination (AUC 0.62)'.

INDEPENDENCE. European multicentre T2D cohort, with no shared sample, recruitment site or authors with P-5 (Daping Hospital / WMU Eye Hospital, China), P-952 (Seventh Affiliated Hospital SYSU, Shenzhen), P-966 (GARD, Korea) or P-105 (review). The same is true against the other candidates: P-224 (Qatar), P-830 (a 2021 synthesis whose search closed before this 2026 study existed) and P-1152 (Morocco). It is a distinct dataset family. On method it is fundus vessel morphometry with regression, close to P-952's fundus-photograph family, but classical statistics rather than HOG+SVM. Not a preprint: a peer-reviewed article in Primary Care Diabetes.

quotes.quote: We found arteriolar tortuosity was associated with MCI in the multivariable analysis (OR 1.44 [95 % CI 1.08–1.92]; the less the tortuosity the higher the risk). When estimating the discriminative ability of the retinal microvascular parameters, we found an AUC of 0.73.

However, only arteriolar tortuosity was associated with MCI in the multivariable analysis (OR 1.44 [95 % CI 1.08–1.92]). We did not find any of the other retinal microvascular parameters to be associated with MCI in the crude or in the multivariable adjusted models (Table 2).

we found an AUC of 0.62 in the model in which we included all retinal microvascular parameters, but when adding the baseline characteristics (age, sex, diabetes duration, severity of diabetic retinopathy, HbA1c, years of education, mean arterial pressure, alcohol consumption and hypoglycemic events during the past six months) to the model the AUC increased to 0.73, which was the best performing model. participants were recruited from eleven clinical sites throughout seven European countries which included Denmark, Italy, Montenegro, Portugal, Spain, The Netherlands and the United Kingdom. Eligible participants were 65 years of age or older with type 2 diabetes with at least five years of diabetes duration.

First, the system for retinal vessel analysis is semiautomatic and requires to be fully automated and if possible incorporated directly in the fundus camara to analyze the vessels directly when the images are taken. Secondly, the discriminability needs to be enhanced to at least an AUC of 0.80 to be considered as a valid.
Lastly, caution should be exercised when interpreting the data presented, as there is a potential for spurious associations due to multiple testing.

Retinal microvascular parameters were considered acceptable, when paired with demographic and systemic variables in regard to their ability to identify people with MCI but still falls short of strong discriminative accuracy.
